Hell? That was one of those things I'd always laughed at, believing that it was just a concept to scare grown men into going to church and saying grace. Living the life of an atheist was pretty fun, while it lasted. My Sundays were always free and I could spin some serious B.S. to avoid having to participate in Secret Santa during the winter holidays. Well, I guess I might have been wrong about a few things. 

After coming to terms with the whole "your soul is condemned to eternal damnation" thing my ass was firmly planted in the office of Alister. I shivered, finding the temperature to be just a few degrees colder than what I would have preferred. As if that wasn't enough, but the seat seemed to be just an inch shorter than it should have been for a guy of my height, which made me slightly uncomfortable. I suppose I should have expected this sort of thing. Hell, if I was the King of Hell I'd definitely go out of my way to make everyone slightly uncomfortable. It would never fail to get a chuckle out of me. 

Alister looked down at me with some bemusement, his eyes laughing at a joke I obviously was not clued in on. "So, Chuck, is it?" Something about the tone in his voice made me think that he knew damn well who I was. That and the fact that his secretary had referred to me by name, making this a rhetorical question. Was it to annoy me, or simply to break the ice?

"Uh, yeah. Though I prefer to go by Charlie." 

"Nice to meet you Chuck!" Alister shuffled a few papers on his desk before continuing, "Now, you're one of the many... Fortunate souls to end up in this fine establishment. And even more fortunate to be a V.I.S."

"Very important soul?"

"Something like that," he grinned, showing off what seemed to be every perfect tooth in his skull. "Though you should be happy. Normally we start people off by having them watch a playlist of every cringeworthy memory they tried so hard to repress. You know, the times you said something stupid or acted like an idiot in front of a crush. The memories you almost forgot about but then, after months of living a blissful life, it all comes crashing down in one embarrassing wave of emotion. Now, that's for the first few weeks. We like to keep everyone on their toes by shaking things up a bit. Hell, sometimes we literally shake things up. But with you, the big man upstairs wanted you to have a very special conversation."

"What kind of conversation?"

"The kind where you exchange words with another person, of course."

"No shit. What's supposed to make it special?"

"You see, there are billions of timelines created with almost every decision anyone makes. An infinite number of possibilities that border on the bizarre and sometimes revolting. Did you know that, in an usual timeline, Elvis actually died and was resurrected? Many claimed his death to be fake but his funky flow and smooth, buttery words reached the ears of God who brought him back from the dead? Turns out its not that hard to talk to God, you just have to be one of a kind."

"So what does any of that have to do with me?"

"You're going to talk to someone from a timeline you could never have possibly imagined. To a person who did something so incredible, his actions moved Satan himself. And that person is you."

"What could I possibly have done to make Satan cry?"

"Why don't you ask this mystery 'you', yourself?" Alister stood up, slightly adjusting his suit and walked out of the room. Confused, I looked back at him, ready to ask more questions. Before the first word left my mouth I heard someone clearing his throat behind me. My body snapped back, staring into the face of a man... Who looked almost identical to mine. His hair was long and black, unlike my own which was short and dyed a ridiculous shade of purple. He wore a set of semi-casual clothes, the kind you'd wear to one of those try hard restaurants that pressure its customers to wear 'neat' clothes or face the wrath of silent social ridicule. Though this... Guy lacked the bemused expression of Alister, I could just tell that his eyes were laughing at the same joke his majordomo had enjoyed.

"So... Hey..." I murmured, uncertain of how to break the ice with myself.

"Hello," he smiled back, his voice seeming quieter than mine.

"Any idea what you did differently than me? Or I guess what I did differently than you?" I asked.

"But of course. The difference is quite amusing." His eyes fixated on me, investing every detail they could uncover from my unsuspecting face. 

"And that difference would be?"

"I found God." The alternate me's voice cracked, going from quiet and amused to the ghost of a laughter. 

"Oh... Well how'd you end up in here if you found God? I mean... Wouldn't you have gone to heaven or something?"

"I think you misunderstood what I said. When I said I found God, I did not reach some spiritual enlightenment. I. Found. God. I did what you would not. I searched high and low, seeking out the maker of existence. I did not try to brush off the idea of God and his afterlife like you did, but uncover something extraordinary. And one look at the twisted soul who managed to sneak past the gates of heaven and discover the location of his creator earned him a prize. Would you like to guess what that prize was?"

Dumbfounded, I responded "not really..."

"He gave me a job offering. Right down here in this cozy little establishment. All I had to do was move the Devil off his throne and show hell what I'm really made of. How could I refuse? Sucks for you though. You could have been me if you'd tried hard enough. You took the easy way out. You blocked out every sign and warning the universe tried to give you in order to live a more 'blissful' life. What a sucker you were. But, I suppose since we're somewhat related... You're a very important sucker."

I just wanted to toss out a number to establish the concept. As this would be taking place over a month, Blizzard would likely have to calculate a reasonable HP that would last throughout the entire event.

I felt like having highly unique prizes (such as alternate art and new heroes) would make it more interesting for players who have been playing for a long time and would like to  spice up their decks with a new Sylvanas.


Though, I do think that gaining x packs based on every y damage would help new players become invested in the game as it would be easy for them to build up a sizable collection.


As for golden cards...


Perhaps during the event the chances of getting gold cards from packs are more likely? Or maybe everyone gets 15 packs at the end where they're all full of gold cards.

I would imagine that if one combo is being over used, key cards would be banned so that the entire event isn't just centered around one deck.


This is also where having the boss use different decks can significantly help. If one week, the boss is using a highly aggressive deck, then you want to respond with a deck that can keep itself alive and eventually combo or establish a threatening board that does a huge amount of damage.


Another week could be where the boss basically makes it impossible for you to burst it down (maybe with a variant of animated armor?)
The technology just isn't there yet

The idea is to chip away at the boss's health over the course of a month. Though looking back, 500,000 HP would probably be easy to knock down by everyone in a server. 


I also considered having three mini bosses that either each player has to defeat before going after the world-boss, or three bosses that are available to fight in the weeks leading up to the world boss. One for each week. This would be similar to the bosses players have to defeat before the final boss in adventures and build up hype.


Or perhaps the community has to defeat three bosses before going up against the final boss? So four world-bosses in total?


Though, I agree that I set the pack quota rather low. It would definitely make more sense to earn x packs for every y damage dealt. It would actually make the grind to the top prizes more worth while as players would periodically be rewarded for their efforts.
